summary.title: Top 10 System Design Interview Questions for Software Engineers
summary.one_liner: You learn ten commonly asked system design interview prompts (URL shortener, video streaming, chat, social feeds, file storage, ride sharing, search type-ahead, rate limiter, proximity search) and the sub-questions interviewers expect you to address for each.
takeaways: Each common system design prompt comes with a list of sub-questions interviewers tend to ask, such as unique ID generation, redirects, and expiry for a URL shortener.
Video and chat designs focus on large-scale storage and distribution, real-time comments, offline handling, push notifications, and encryption.
Feed, social graph, and ride-matching designs stress efficient storage, fan-out for celebrities, and handling millions of location updates per second.
Rate limiter and type-ahead designs cover distributed counting, throttling strategies, data freshness, and crawl prioritization.
The article is a short prompt list rather than worked solutions, and it recommends external prep resources such as Grokking the Modern System Design Interview.
summary.summary: This HackerNoon article, by a co-founder of Educative, lists ten frequently asked system design interview questions for software engineers. Each entry names a well-known service (such as TinyURL, YouTube, WhatsApp, Dropbox, Uber, or a web crawler) and gives bullet points on what an interviewer wants to hear about, such as storage, scaling, real-time updates, and permissions. It does not provide full worked answers. The page closes with a couple of recommended prep books, including Grokking the Modern System Design Interview and Coderust.
